newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's CIADEA sets output stoppages.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's CIADEA sets output stoppages.

text.p: Argentina's CIADEA SA, licensee of France's Renault, halted output for several days this month due to autoparts supply disruptions and a fall in Brazilian demand for cars, a top company official was quoted as saying Wednesday.

La Nacion newspaper said CIADEA's manager for Industrial Relations Juan Manuel Lardizabal argued one of the reasons to suspend production was a lower demand in Brazil as a result of that country's new policy of subsidizing its car industry.

CIADEA announced this week it halted production at its Cordoba plant on March 6 and 7, will stop making its Trafic van on March 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 17 and 31 and also will interrupt production of its small car Clio on March 31.
It said the measure was "exceptional" and owed to certain autoparts supply disruptions and a revised export program.
However press reports quoted unions as saying one of the reasons for halting output were accumulating stocks the company was unable to sell.
Lardizabal rebuked the unions's claims and said that 2,200 out of its 3,600 employees were suspended last week, La Nacion said.
No company officials were immediately available for comment.
CIADEA said staff will be granted an extraordinary "non salary" compensation equivalent to 75 percent of their respective salaries.
With more than 6,000 vehicles made in February, CIADEA ranked third that month in local car production after Volkswagen and Ford.
In 1996 the company earned $61 million versus a net loss of $17.5 million in 1995.
